source.title: What Does the Weight Norm Control in Grokking? Logit-Scale Mediation under Cross-Entropy

page_placements.theme: Weight norm is an incomplete control variable

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study intervenes on norm and logit scale to refine the account of grokking delay, and tests whether a numerical-precision artifact explains some results.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own modular-addition experiments. Cited results from other studies are not recorded as rows. Raw cells from the norm–temperature grid are omitted under the 60-row cap; the grid’s regression summaries are retained.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own modular-addition experiments (MLPs and a no-LayerNorm transformer). It measures memorization time and grokking time under clamped norm and output-temperature interventions. It argues that the norm-delay link under cross-entropy runs through effective logit scale. A float64 audit bears on the numerical-artifact account (V7).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Under cross-entropy, the norm-induced delay is mediated mainly by effective logit scale and softmax saturation (recovery 0.83/0.89; logit scale R²=0.97). Under MSE the norm effect is smaller and runs through another route. The float32 collapse at ρ=1.25 caused a spurious early grok, not the delay. Same-state forks show the delay tracks the held norm value, not the clamp operation. The transformer corroborates qualitatively.
record.recipe_differences: Uses modular addition and grokking-time accuracy thresholds, but adds clamped norm, output-temperature mediation, norm–temperature grids, same-state forks, and a float64 audit rather than reproducing the original unmodified training setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The effect depends on loss: cross-entropy shows strong logit-scale mediation, while MSE does not. Temperature changes delay substantially while largely sparing memorization under cross-entropy. Float precision matters at ρ=1.25 but not at ρ=1.15. The no-LayerNorm transformer shows the direction of the temperature effect, but its logit dynamics are noisier. Layer allocation at fixed total norm also changes delay, with embedding capacity as a confound.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed total norm, shifting mass between embedding and readout changes Tgrok by up to 2.2× (p=59) and 1.7× (p=97), while effective logit scale barely moves. The authors attribute this to an embedding-capacity confound.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How the weight norm is allocated across layers, not just the total norm, affects the grokking delay.

fits_no_version.finding: Under cross-entropy the grokking delay is set by the effective logit scale (softmax saturation). Output temperature at fixed norm moves the delay without changing memorization time.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proximal variable controlling grokking delay under cross-entropy is the logit scale, not the weight norm.

record.problems: The quantitative mediation and collapse estimates are from MLPs at two moduli; the transformer result is qualitative. The effective logit scale in the collapse regression is measured at grokking and is endogenous. The recovery-fraction CI holds the logit curve fixed and excludes interpolation uncertainty on the logit axis. MSE's residual mechanism is not characterized. The same-state comparison uses one fork point and one dose. At ρ=1.25, float32 results are softmax-collapse-confounded.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the 24 individual ρ×τ grid cells in Appendix C, Table 7; their aggregate regression results are retained in r25-r26 and the temperature-sweep cells are represented in r01-r12. No other reported result relevant to the tested versions was omitted.

untested.parts: Training-set size is fixed at 40%, so the claim that the delay grows as the training set shrinks is untested. Test-accuracy trajectories at chance are not shown.
Untested: circuit efficiency as such, a critical dataset size, ungrokking, and results from varying weight decay.
Adaptive-optimizer instabilities (e.g. slingshot) are not tested. Only the float32/float64 softmax-collapse case at p=59 is tested.
The paper says it uses the Fourier progress measure but reports no progress-measure results.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V7 'supports' label for r42 is reversed: float32 collapse accelerated grokking. V5 'challenges' is too strong, since the study does not test circuit efficiency or ungrokking and shows low norm speeds grokking; it is recast as supports plus limits_scope. The layer-allocation rows are moved to fits_no_version. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: Tests delayed generalization on modular-addition tasks using training-accuracy and test-accuracy thresholds, but does not report full accuracy trajectories showing test accuracy at chance, nor vary training-set size to test whether smaller sets take longer.
No gradual circuit-formation or memorizing-component-removal result is reported; the paper does not report progress measures anticipating the accuracy jump.
No non-algorithmic datasets or initialization-scale/lazy-to-rich sweep is tested.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning is tested.

Tests whether norm-related delay is mediated by logit scale and whether that relation depends on loss. Does not test whether a circuit is more efficient, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below that size.
Does not compare whether independent runs converge to the same identifiable algorithm.
Tests float32 versus float64 softmax-collapse effects at two norm doses. Does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities generally.

relationships.condition: Cross-entropy MLP (p=59, 97), no-LayerNorm transformer (p=59), and free fork arms
relationships.reason: Grokking comes thousands of steps after memorization, e.g. Tmem 175 vs Tgrok 3675 (r01), 12/12 seeds. Rows r01-r12, r27-r40.
relationships.display_finding: All 12 seeds grokked after memorization, with one example memorizing at step 175 and grokking at step 3,675.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Cross-entropy MLP (p=59, 97), no-LayerNorm transformer (p=59), and free fork arms
source_check.reason: Tables 5, 8 and 10 support delayed generalization in these settings; r02–r12 and r33–r40 capture the timing results. Training-set-size dependence is untested.

relationships.reason: The delay is much shorter under MSE; at p=97 it is 250-438 steps against Tmem 600-975 (r19-r24). The lag depends on the loss choice.
relationships.display_finding: At p=97, MSE produced delays of 250–438 steps, compared with memorization times of 600–975 steps.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: Restrict this condition group to p=97: r19–r24 have delays of 250–438 steps against Tmem=600–975. The p=59 MSE results retain clear delays, including r14 with delay=1875 and Tmem=350, and warrant a separate supporting group.

relationships.condition: Cross-entropy MLP dose response across five moduli, same-state forks, and transformer
relationships.reason: A higher held norm lengthens the delay (α>0 at all moduli, r43-r47; 3.4× norm-up, r02, r08, r28). From an identical state the raised arm is 3.27-3.36× slower and free norm decay groks faster (r33-r40).
relationships.display_finding: Higher held norms lengthened delays across all five moduli, with norm increases producing approximately 3.4-fold delays; from identical states, raised-norm runs were 3.27–3.36 times slower, while free norm decay accelerated grokking.

source_check.label: supports
